items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: "Bass" Hill had told me that Norman would take care of that end.

ctx.x: We did six numbers in which one featured the three trumpets on "Sweet Georgia Brown" and one featured Buck and I on a number we called B.C. and B.C. and it's very easy to see the connection between the title and the two of us.

"Bass" Hill and Norman Lester arrived in Paris a couple of days before we left for Bern which was the 24th of November. Fred Palmer came in from Italy and we opened in the Chikito the 26th with nothing but head numbers. I had, however, bought some music stands with my initials B.C. on them, but Norman had not arranged anything before leaving New York, and I had not picked up on any orchestrations from publishers in Paris because "Bass" Hill had told me that Norman would take care of that end. I had made my first…

& So there we were, with these nice looking stands of light/dark blue with golden sprayed B.C. on them and not the first sheet of music on them. But we made out alright because the one thing that Norman Lester knew was any number that was ever popular in jazz and most of them that were not. He also knew the original keys and the names of the composers. I had never played a gig with Norman, so I didn't know what style he played until we rehearsed the day before we opened at the Chikito.
